title: One-Pot Creamy Corn & White Bean Pasta
description: Pasta, sweet corn, and white beans cook in one pot with a little milk and Parmesan for an inexpensive creamy supper.
substitutions: Use chickpeas instead of white beans.
Use frozen peas instead of corn.
Use an additional 1/2 cup broth instead of milk for a less creamy version.

cookSteps.text: Add 8 ounces short pasta, 3 cups vegetable broth, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder to a large pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a lively simmer and cook for about 10 minutes, stirring often.
Stir in 1 drained can white beans and 1 1/2 cups frozen corn. Cook 5 minutes more, stirring, until the pasta is tender and most of the broth is absorbed.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in 1/2 cup milk, 1/2 cup grated Parmesan, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper. Cook 2–3 minutes until creamy, adding a splash of water if needed.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat with a splash of milk or water.

title: Tuna, Cucumber & White Bean Pitas
description: Tuna and white beans make a filling no-cook pita filling with crisp cucumber and a simple lemony dressing.
substitutions: Use plain Greek yogurt instead of mayonnaise.
Use chopped celery instead of cucumber.
Serve in wraps or on toast instead of pitas.

cookSteps.text: In a bowl, gently mix 1 drained can tuna, 1 drained can white beans, 1 cup diced cucumber, 3 tablespoons mayonnaise, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.
Divide the filling among 4 pita pockets and serve right away.

storage: Refrigerate the filling up to 2 days. Fill pitas just before eating.

title: Leftover Mashed Potato & Broccoli Waffles
description: Leftover mashed potatoes and cooked broccoli turn crisp at the edges in a waffle iron for an easy savory food-rescue meal.
substitutions: Use cooked peas or finely chopped spinach instead of broccoli.
Use Monterey Jack or mozzarella instead of cheddar.

steps.text: Cook in the waffle iron until crisp.

cookSteps.text: Preheat the waffle iron. Mix 2 cups cold mashed potatoes, 1 cup finely chopped cooked broccoli, 2 eggs, 3/4 cup shredded cheddar, 1/4 cup flour, and 1/4 teaspoon garlic powder.

Lightly oil the waffle iron. Add enough potato mixture to cover the center without overfilling, close, and cook until deeply golden and crisp, about 6–8 minutes per batch. Repeat with the remaining mixture.

storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days. Reheat in a toaster oven or dry skillet to restore crispness.

title: Small-Batch Oatmeal Jam Bars
description: A six-serving pan of buttery oat crumble sandwiches whatever jam is already in the refrigerator.
substitutions: Use any flavor of jam or preserves.
Use quick oats if that is what you have; the texture will be softer.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F and lightly grease a small loaf pan. Mix 3/4 cup oats, 1/2 cup flour, 1/4 cup brown sugar, a pinch of salt, and 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon if using. Stir in 4 tablespoons melted butter until crumbly.
Press about two-thirds of the crumble firmly into the pan. Spread 1/3 cup jam over it, leaving a small border, then scatter the remaining crumble on top.
Bake for 25 minutes until the top is golden and the jam bubbles at the edges. Cool before cutting into 6 bars.

storage: Keep covered at room temperature for 2 days or refrigerate up to 5 days.
